full_bands.model: Heisenberg kagome AFM + easy-axis Kani=0.05 (gaps flat band, isolates bands)
full_bands.interpretation: Each magnon eigenvector projects predominantly onto a single lab axis; one band stays out-of-plane (z) dominant and two stay in-plane (x/y) dominant across the BZ. Purity is highest near Gamma (k=0, the paper's regime) and degrades smoothly at large |k| as the sublattice amplitudes mix, quantifying the finite-k robustness of the paper's k=0 orthogonal-polarization claim.

berry_thermal_hall.method: Fukui-Hatsugai-Suzuki plaquette, BdG g-metric inner product
berry_thermal_hall.model: Heisenberg kagome AFM + easy-axis Kani=0.05, NO Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya
berry_thermal_hall.interpretation: SYMMETRY ARGUMENT: the DMI-free kagome AFM (only Heisenberg exchange + collinear-plane 120-deg order + easy-axis anisotropy) is invariant under an effective time-reversal (combined with a spin rotation / mirror), so the magnon Berry curvature is forced to zero and the intrinsic magnon thermal Hall conductivity VANISHES. NUMERICAL CHECK: the two in-plane magnon bands are degenerate / cross along BZ symmetry lines (min direct gap = 4.44e-16), so the single-band Fukui-Hatsugai-Suzuki flux is gauge-ill-defined and SATURATES at |F|=pi on 1% of plaquettes -- the branch-cut ceiling, NOT real curvature. The raw_* fields are reported transparently as artifacts. A well-defined, nonzero magnon thermal Hall requires adding an out-of-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term D_z to lift the degeneracy and imprint finite scalar spin chirality -- absent in this paper's model. This bounds the topological consequence of the band structure: for lund2021's Hamiltonian it is zero.

claim_check.claim: Three spin-wave bands of kagome AF pump spin currents with mutually orthogonal polarizations
claim_check.polarization_axes: x, y, z (eigenvectors of diagonal K)
claim_check.note: Paper is spin-PUMPING (not thermal Hall). The 'three bands' are the k=0 uniform-precession resonance modes; their polarizations are the eigenvectors of the diagonal anisotropy matrix K=diag(K1,K1,K2), hence mutually orthogonal (x,y,z).

kresolved_fixed_axis_scan.note: Along a generic off-axis direction the two IN-PLANE bands rotate their polarization from (x,y) at Gamma toward (k_hat, k_hat_perp). This is a rotation WITHIN the xy-plane: planarity stays 1 and the triad stays mutually orthogonal. Along high-symmetry axes (kx=0 or ky=0) the in-plane block stays diagonal so bands remain pure x/y.

kresolved_verdict.scaled: k=0 uniform modes  ->  full k-resolved eigenvectors D(k) over BZ
kresolved_verdict.observable_before: polarizations orthogonal x/y/z verified ONLY at k=0
kresolved_verdict.finding: The three magnon-band polarizations remain MUTUALLY ORTHOGONAL across the ENTIRE Brillouin zone (max Gram off-diagonal ~1e-16), not just at Gamma. This is protected by the block structure of the continuum dynamical matrix D(k): (i) the z component decouples (k is in-plane), so the z-band stays perfectly z-polarized for all k; (ii) the in-plane 2x2 block is real-symmetric, so its two eigenvectors are exactly orthogonal and remain in the xy-plane. The orthogonal-polarization spin-pumping structure is therefore NOT a k=0 accident -- it survives at finite k.
kresolved_verdict.honest_caveat: The two in-plane bands are DEGENERATE at Gamma (w0_x = w0_y = 0.9487), so their individual x/y labels are gauge-dependent there -- only their 2D span is physical. Any finite k in a generic direction lifts this degeneracy and snaps the two eigenvectors onto (k_hat, k_hat_perp) essentially immediately (fixed-axis purity drops below 0.9 by |k|~0.006 along a 30deg cut). This is an in-plane rotation of degenerate partners only: it never mixes in the z-band and never breaks the mutual orthogonality of the triad. It does NOT affect the paper's pumping claim, which is driven by a spatially-UNIFORM (k=0) field. Along the high-symmetry axes (kx=0 or ky=0) the in-plane block stays diagonal so the bands remain exactly pure x / y. The k* = sqrt(K1/g) ~ 0.548/a scale instead sets where the DISPERSIVE splitting of the in-plane pair becomes comparable to the exchange stiffness.
